stories.headline: Russia launches massive drone and missile barrage killing up to 16 across Ukraine, Dnipro hit hardest
stories.summary: Russian forces launched one of their largest recent attacks overnight April 24–25, deploying over 600 drones and 47 missiles that pounded Dnipro for up to 20 hours. At least 10 people were killed and dozens wounded; Odesa and Kharkiv were also struck. PM Svyrydenko pledged government support for Dnipro.

stories.headline: Ukraine pushes for direct Zelensky–Putin summit, asks Turkey to host talks as US mediation stalls
stories.summary: Ukraine formally asked Turkey to host a meeting between Presidents Zelensky and Putin as peace negotiations stalled amid the US-Iran war absorbing Washington's attention. FM Sybiha said Kyiv would accept any neutral venue except Russia or Belarus, while Zelensky simultaneously called Trump envoys' repeated Moscow visits without Kyiv stops 'disrespectful.' Trump confirmed he was holding calls with both leaders.

stories.headline: Chernobyl 40th anniversary: Zelensky accuses Russia of 'nuclear terrorism,' IAEA signs reconstruction deal
stories.summary: Ukraine marked the 40th anniversary of the Chornobyl disaster with Zelensky calling Russia's attacks near the site 'nuclear terrorism,' warning a drone hit the confinement structure last year. The IAEA signed an energy reconstruction agreement with Ukraine, the EBRD flagged a €500m need to repair the damaged shelter, and EU energy officials visited Kyiv. PM Svyrydenko also noted risks from Russian occupation of Zaporizhzhia NPP.

stories.headline: Syrskyi conducts Pokrovsk frontline visit, orders logistics inspection, meets NATO and EU military chiefs
stories.summary: Commander-in-Chief Syrskyi visited the Pokrovsk sector — the most intensively attacked front with 688 Russian attacks in April — and ordered reinforcement of units. He separately met with NATO and EU Military Committee chairs Dragone and Clancy, announced $25.5 billion in estimated Russian losses from Ukrainian strikes, and warned Russia is advancing across nearly the entire front while its air defense is running short of missiles.

stories.headline: NATO-EU mutual defense debate intensifies as Trump divides allies into 'good' and 'bad' lists over Iran war
stories.summary: The Trump administration reportedly compiled lists ranking NATO allies by compliance with US Iran war operations, with the Pentagon considering punishments including troop relocations and threats to Spain and the UK. EU leaders simultaneously discussed activating Article 42.7 mutual defense clauses independent of NATO, and Polish PM Tusk warned Russia could attack a NATO member within months. These debates ran parallel to the Cyprus EU summit.

stories.headline: Budanov at Kyiv Security Forum: Ukraine not losing, AI drone breakthrough imminent, no territorial concessions
stories.summary: Head of the Presidential Office Kyrylo Budanov addressed the 18th Kyiv Security Forum, declaring Ukraine is 'definitely not losing' but needs an AI-driven technological leap to win the drone race. He revealed Ukraine has near-ready autonomous drone systems that will 'surprise' Russia, opposed civilian gun legalization following a recent Kyiv shooting, and reiterated that no Ukrainians will accept loss of any territory in peace talks.

stories.headline: Zelensky visits Saudi Arabia and Azerbaijan, signs security and defense export deals across Gulf region
stories.summary: President Zelensky made his second visit to Saudi Arabia in under a month, meeting Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to advance air defense, energy, and infrastructure partnerships. He then traveled to Baku where he signed six agreements including security cooperation with Azerbaijan's President Aliyev. Ukraine has now signed 10-year defense export agreements with Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Qatar focused on drone warfare expertise.
